title: Augmented vertex-star limits and the Cech right Kan extension condition
statement:
Use universes, small ordinary nerves, quasicategories, coherent transformations and limiting cones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\Delta_+$ have the finite linearly ordered sets, including $\varnothing=[-1]$, and all monotone maps, and let $j:\Delta_+^{\leq0}\hookrightarrow\Delta_+$ include $\varnothing$ and $[0]$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory and $U:N(\Delta_+)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ an augmented simplicial object. Put $B=U_{-1}$, $A=U_0$ and $a:A\to B$ its augmentation. For $n\geq0$ let $V_n$ have objects $b,v_0,\ldots,v_n$, with exactly one nonidentity arrow $v_i\to b$ for each $i$. The vertex-star diagram takes $b$ to $B$, each $v_i$ to $A$, and each arrow to $a$. The restrictions $\{i\}\hookrightarrow[n]$ and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow[n]$ specify a coherent cone on it with apex $U_n$.
The object $U$ is a right Kan extension of $Uj^{\mathrm{op}}$ along $N(j^{\mathrm{op}})$ if and only if every one of these specified vertex-star cones is limiting. Here right Kan extension is understood in the pointwise coherent sense: at each object $[n]$ the prescribed extension cone on the opposite of the comma category of maps $j(d)\to[n]$ is limiting; the objects $d$ are $[-1]$ and $[0]$. Whenever $\mathcal C$ admits pullbacks, the limit of the vertex-star diagram is the iterated pullback of $n+1$ copies of $A\to B$, with its vertex and augmentation projections; for $n=0$ it is $A$. If every specified square $U_{n+1}\to U_n$ over $A\to B$, using the first $n+1$ vertices above and the last vertex at left, is cartesian, these vertex-star cones are limiting. Under their canonical comparisons, the operator $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ induces the map selecting coordinates $\theta(0),\ldots,\theta(m)$, and these identifications retain all higher simplicial compatibilities of $U$. No realization, groupoid, effective-epimorphism, or colimit hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.2.11 and its proof, printed pp.541–543: the vertex slice I([n]) and Cech right Kan extension; iterated-pullback limit of the finite star via the gluing of its edges. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states the coherent assertion.

proof.text: By the stated pointwise convention for right Kan extension, the right Kan extension condition is the limiting condition on the opposite of $(j\downarrow[n])$. For $n\geq0$, this comma category has one object $([-1],\varnothing\to[n])$ and one object $([0],i)$ for each vertex $i$ of $[n]$. Its only nonidentity arrows go from the empty-set object to the vertex objects: they are induced by the unique map $[-1]\to[0]$. Consequently its opposite, not the comma category itself, is $V_n$, and restricting $U$ gives exactly the specified vertex-star cone, including its coherence. At $n=-1$ the comma category has just the identity of $[-1]$; the prescribed cone is the identity cone on $B$, which is limiting by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]: for every $x$ the cone-induced comparison $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,B)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,\mathcal C)}(\Delta_{\Delta^0}x,B)$ is the identity after the defining identification $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,\mathcal C)=\mathcal C$. Thus the pointwise conditions at all objects of $\Delta_+$ are equivalent to the asserted conditions for $n\geq0$.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.2.11 and proof, pp. 541–543; identification of the pointwise comma category with the vertex star.

proof.text:
Use the limit duals of [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit] and [lem-coef-infinity-colimit-gluing]. Concretely apply those statements to $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and opposite indexing shapes: ordinal reversal exchanges inner horn $i$ with inner horn $r-i$, preserves degreewise injectivity and degreewise pushouts, and exchanges the defined cones and cocones. Thus the colimit-gluing statement gives limits on a union of shapes from the pullback of their three restricted limits, with the induced coherent cone and its projections. It requires only that particular pullback, not all finite limits or a terminal object. The initial vertex of the arrow shape $V_0=(v_0\to b)$ gives its limit $A$, with legs $1_A$ and $a$, by the final-index statement applied oppositely. In every simplicial degree there is an actual pushout
$$N(V_{n+1})=N(V_n)\amalg_{\{b\}}\Delta^1_{v_{n+1},b}:$$
there are no composable nonidentity arrows in a star, so every nondegenerate simplex belongs to one of these edges, and their intersection is exactly $b$. The inclusion of $b$ into the new edge is degreewise injective. If the old limiting cone has apex $L_n$, the three restricted limits are $L_n$, $B$ and $A$; their comparison cospan is $L_n\to B\leftarrow A$, where the first leg is the old augmentation projection and the second is $a$. Gluing therefore makes $L_{n+1}=L_n\times_B A$ a limiting apex for the enlarged star, with precisely the old vertex projections after $L_{n+1}\to L_n$, the new projection to $A$, and their coherent common projection to $B$. When $\mathcal C$ admits pullbacks this induction starts at $L_0=A$ and constructs the asserted iterated pullback limits for every $n$.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.2.11, printed pp.541–543, vertex slices I([n]); Proposition 4.4.2.2 and Remark 4.4.2.3, printed p.296, applied oppositely to the displayed union of stars. Agent expansion of the edge-by-edge gluing argument.

proof.text: Now assume only the specified cartesian squares, without assuming other pullbacks exist in $\mathcal C$. The specified $V_0$ cone has apex $U_0=A$ and is the limit cone just identified. Inductively suppose the specified $V_n$ cone with apex $U_n$ is limiting. The hypothesis gives a pullback cone with apex $U_{n+1}$ for the cospan $U_n\to B\leftarrow A$; [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion] identifies its mapping-space comparison as an equivalence, retaining the square's specified coherence. Apply the limit dual of [lem-coef-infinity-colimit-gluing] to the same pushout of shapes as in step 2, with this particular pullback. Its induced limiting cone is the specified cone from $U$: on $N(V_n)$ its legs are restriction to the first $n+1$ vertices, on the new edge its leaf leg is restriction to the last vertex, and on their intersection its leg is the augmentation. The coherence joining these restrictions is exactly that of the assumed square, all obtained by restricting the same simplicial diagram $U$. Thus gluing proves this specified $V_{n+1}$ cone limiting. This induction includes $n=0$ (the square $U_1\to A$ over $A\to B$) and proves the claim for every degree. Step 1 then gives the right Kan extension condition.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.2.11 proof, pp. 541–543; induction using the cartesian comparison squares.

proof.text:
Assume the specified cones are limiting, as in the preceding clauses, and write $F_m:N(V_m)\to\mathcal C$ for the star diagram. The functor $s_\theta:V_m\to V_n$ sends $b$ to $b$ and $v_r$ to $v_{\theta(r)}$, so $F_m=F_nN(s_\theta)$. Restricting the specified $V_n$ cone along $s_\theta$ gives a full coherent cone $c_\theta$ on $F_m$ with apex $U_n$. The simplicial map $U(\theta):U_n\to U_m$ compares this cone to the limiting $V_m$ cone: its $r$-th leaf component is the $\theta(r)$-th projection since $\theta\iota_r=\iota_{\theta(r)}$, and its central component and all the edge compatibility homotopies are obtained by restricting $U$ along the augmentation maps. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], composition with the limiting $V_m$ cone gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(U_n,U_m)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(V_m),\mathcal C)}(\Delta_{V_m}U_n,F_m).$$
Its homotopy fiber over $c_\theta$ is contractible. Hence $U(\theta)$, together with its specified cone comparison, is the coordinate-selection map up to contractible coherent choice. This argument uses the full cone, including its edge homotopies, rather than just equalities in the homotopy category. Here is the higher compatibility explicitly. Given a string $[n_0]\to\cdots\to[n_k]$ and a vertex $r\in[n_0]$, let $r_i$ be its image in $[n_i]$. These data define an ordinary functor $[k]\times[2]\to\Delta_+$ whose value on $(i,0)$ is $[-1]$, on $(i,1)$ is $[0]$, and on $(i,2)$ is $[n_i]$. Its horizontal maps are the empty-set inclusion and the vertex inclusion $r_i$, and its vertical maps are identities in the first two columns and the given monotone maps in the last. The defining squares commute because the vertices $r_i$ were propagated along the string. Restricting $U$ along the opposite nerve of this functor supplies the full parameter family of augmentation and vertex cone comparisons, including their compatibility triangles. Faces delete or compose the same monotone maps and degeneracies insert identities, so restrictions along every face and degeneracy give the corresponding family for that shorter or repeated string. Applying this to all vertices and all subchains covers every coordinate. Thus the original coherent diagram supplies the coordinate comparisons and their compatibilities in every dimension simultaneously. One may take the already limiting $U_n$ cones as the iterated-pullback models themselves; comparisons with other models are equivalences in the contractible space of limiting cones supplied by the same cited node. This proves the asserted compatibility without replacing the coherent diagram by unrelated maps chosen in each degree.
